title: One-Step Equations: Building the Inverse Move
preview: Walk from x + 4 = 10 through subtraction, multiplication, division, negative results, and negative coefficients — one variation at a time. Enrichment adds fractional and decimal coefficients.

body.goal: Students see one-step equation solving as 'undo the operation that's happening to x' across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division — including when negatives or fractions appear.
body.launch: Run the warm-up to make sure inverse arithmetic is hot. Then start the slice. Resist explaining 'subtract from both sides' until a student says it.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up by computing the inverse arithmetic before we use it inside an equation.

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Negative result — anchor before they see it inside an equation.

steps.teacherNote: Switch to subtraction — undone by addition.
Switch to multiplication — undone by division.
Switch to division. Notice the stacked fraction notation.
Negative result emerges. Don't pre-warn — let the pattern do the work.
Negative coefficient — divide by a negative.
Negative divisor. Multiply both sides by -2.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Fractional coefficient — multiply both sides by 2 (or by the reciprocal).
Decimal coefficient — divide by 0.4 or rewrite as 2/5.
Fractional constant on the same side as x.

body.consolidation: Bring the class back. Ask: 'In every problem we did, what was the move? Can you say it in one sentence?' Steer toward: 'Do the opposite of whatever is happening to x.' Then ask: 'When did the answer come out negative? Where did the negative come from?'
